﴿إن الله عالم غيب السماوات والأرض﴾: إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); the Name of Majesty is the noun of inna; عالم: the khabar (predicate) of inna; غيب: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and غيب is itself muḍāf; السماوات: muḍāf ilayhi; الأرض: conjoined to السماوات.
﴿إنه عليم بذات الصدور﴾: إنه: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle, and the hāʾ is a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna; عليم: the khabar of inna; بذات: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿عليم﴾; الصدور: muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t:
﴿هو الذي جعلكم خلائف في الأرض﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; هو: mubtadaʾ (subject); الذي: a relative noun in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; جعلكم: a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); خلائف: second mafʿūl bihi; في الأرض: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خلائف﴾ or to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿خلائف﴾; the clause ﴿جعلكم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي, with no grammatical position.
﴿فمن كفر فعليه كفره﴾: الفاء: resumptive; من: a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ; كفر: a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); الفاء: linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); عليه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; كفره: a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the nominal clause ﴿عليه كفره﴾ is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the clause ﴿فمن كفر...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿ولا يزيد الكافرين كفرهم عند ربهم إلا مقتا﴾: الواو: conjunctive; لا: negating; يزيد: an imperfect verb; الكافرين: a fronted mafʿūl bihi; كفرهم: a delayed fāʿil; عند: an adverb (ẓarf) attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ربهم: ﴿رب﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is a pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; إلا: a particle of restriction (adāt ḥaṣr); مقتًا: second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿يزيد﴾; the clause is conjoined to the one before it.
﴿ولا يزيد الكافرين كفرهم إلا خسارا﴾: الواو: conjunctive; لا: negating; يزيد: an imperfect verb; الكافرين: a fronted mafʿūl bihi; كفرهم: a delayed fāʿil; إلا: a particle of restriction; خسارا: second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿يزيد﴾; the clause is conjoined to the one before it.

muyesser-irab:40-40.t:
﴿قل أرأيتم شركاءكم الذين تدعون من دون الله﴾: قل: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun implied as "أنت"; ﴿أرأيتم﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, and رأيتم is a verb and its fāʿil; ﴿أرأيتم﴾ has been made to carry the meaning of "inform me", and on this basis it takes two objects; شركاءكم: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿أرأيتم﴾; الذين: a relative noun, naʿt (adjective); تدعون: an imperfect verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿تدعون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿الذين﴾, with no grammatical position. The returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted; it is the object of تدعون, i.e. "those whom you call upon (تدعونهم)". ﴿من دون﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied object of تدعون; the Name of Majesty: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿أروني﴾: an imperative verb; the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil, the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ of the speaker is mafʿūl bihi. The clause ﴿أروني﴾ is parenthetical with no grammatical position, coming as a parenthesis between the verb ﴿رأيتم﴾ and its second object, the clause ﴿ماذا خلقوا...﴾; or the clause ﴿أروني ماذا خلقوا من الأرض﴾ is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from أرأيتم, as though it were said: "Inform me about your partners: show me what thing they have created of the earth?".
﴿ماذا خلقوا من الأرض﴾: ماذا: an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi of ﴿خلق﴾; خلقوا: a verb and its fāʿil; or ﴿ما﴾ is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and ﴿ذا﴾ is a relative noun, the khabar (predicate) of ﴿ما﴾, and the clause ﴿خلقوا﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The returning pronoun is omitted; it is the object of خلق, i.e. "what is it that they created (خلقوه)". من الأرض: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خلقوا﴾ or to an omitted ḥāl from the object of خلق; the clause ﴿ماذا خلقوا...﴾ is in the position of accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿أرأيتم﴾ if the clause ﴿أروني﴾ is parenthetical; or the clause ﴿ماذا خلقوا...﴾ is in the position of accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿أروني﴾, the matter being a case of contention between governors (tanāzuʿ), in which the second verb has been made to govern.
﴿أم لهم شرك في السماوات﴾: أم: a conjunction, and it is the disjoined (munqaṭiʿa) am, in the sense of "nay" together with the hamza of disapproving interrogation, i.e. "nay, do they have a share in the heavens?". ﴿لهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; شرك: a delayed mubtadaʾ; في السماوات: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt of ﴿شرك﴾.
﴿أم آتيناهم كتابا فهم على بينة منه﴾: conjoined to what precedes; آتيناهم: a verb, its fāʿil and first mafʿūl bihi; كتابًا: second mafʿūl bihi; الفاء: a conjunction; هم: mubtadaʾ; على بينة: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar; منه: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt of ﴿بينة﴾.
﴿بل إن يعد الظالمون بعضهم بعضا إلا غرورا﴾: بل: a particle of transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī); إن: negating; يعد: an imperfect verb; الظالمون: fāʿil; بعضهم: badal (substitute) from ﴿الظالمون﴾, a badal of part for whole; بعضًا: the object of ﴿يعد﴾; إلا: a particle of restriction (adāt ḥaṣr); غرورًا: second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿يعد﴾, or a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "except a promise of delusion".

muyesser-irab:41-41.t:
﴿إن الله يمسك السماوات والأرض أن تزولا﴾: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position; إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); الله: the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna; يمسك: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "هو"; السماوات: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الأرض: conjoined to السماوات; the clause ﴿يمسك السماوات والأرض﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of inna; أن: maṣdariyya, governing the subjunctive; تزولا: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by the dropping of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن تزولا﴾ is mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) with an omitted muḍāf understood, i.e. "out of aversion to their ceasing"; or ﴿يمسك﴾ has been made to carry the meaning of "prevents", so the interpreted maṣdar is a second mafʿūl bihi; or it is by removal of the preposition, i.e. "He prevents them from ceasing (من أن تزولا)", the preposition and its genitive ﴿من أن تزولا﴾ being attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يمسك﴾; or it is accusative as a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from السماوات والأرض, i.e. "He prevents their ceasing".
﴿ولئن زالتا إن أمسكهما من أحد من بعده﴾: الواو: conjunctive; the lām: preparing for an oath (mūṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); إن: conditional; زالتا: a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); إن: negating; أمسكهما: a past verb, the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi, and the mīm and alif are the sign of the dual; من: a redundant preposition (ḥarf jarr ṣila); أحد: fāʿil of ﴿أمسكهما﴾, genitive in form by ﴿من﴾, nominative in position; من بعده: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أحد﴾; the clause ﴿إن أمسكهما...﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the answer to an implied oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath; the clause ﴿لئن زالتا﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿إن الله يمسك السماوات...﴾.
﴿إنه كان حليما غفورا﴾: إنه: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle, and the hāʾ is a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna; كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) verb, the noun of kāna latent, implied as "هو"; حليما: the khabar of kāna; غفورا: a second khabar of ﴿كان﴾; the clause ﴿كان حليما غفورا﴾ is the khabar of inna, and the clause ﴿إنه كان...﴾ is causal (taʿlīliyya).

muyesser-irab:42-42.t:
﴿وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم لئن جاءهم نذير ليكونن أهدى من إحدى الأمم﴾: الواو: resumptive; ﴿أقسموا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿بالله﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أقسموا﴾; ﴿جهد﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "they swore by Allah striving hard in their oaths", or standing in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it has the meaning of the maṣdar, the sense being "they swore an oath of utmost effort in swearing". ﴿أيمانهم﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لئن﴾: the lām is preparing for an oath (mūṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam), and ﴿إن﴾ is conditional; ﴿جاءهم﴾: a past verb, the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the mīm is the sign of the plural; ﴿نذير﴾: fāʿil; ﴿ليكونن﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and ﴿يكونن﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, which is omitted because of the succession of like letters; the wāw of the plural, omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the noun of yakūnu, and the doubled nūn is for emphasis; ﴿أهدى﴾: the khabar (predicate) of yakūnu; ﴿من إحدى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أهدى﴾; ﴿الأمم﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿وأقسموا بالله...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿فلما جاءهم نذير ما زادهم إلا نفورا﴾: الفاء: conjunctive; ﴿لما﴾: a temporal adverb meaning "when" (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya), or a linking particle containing the sense of a condition; ﴿جاءهم﴾: a past verb, the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi and the mīm is the sign of the plural; ﴿نذير﴾: fāʿil; ﴿ما﴾: negating; ﴿زادهم﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), implied as "هو", the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi and the mīm is the sign of the plural; ﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (adāt ḥaṣr); ﴿نفورًا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿ما زادهم...﴾ is the answer to ﴿لَمّا﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:43-43.t:
﴿استكبارا في الأرض ومكر السيئ﴾: استكبارًا: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for the sake of arrogance", or badal (substitute) from ﴿نفورًا﴾, or ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "in the state of being arrogant". في الأرض: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿استكبارًا﴾; مكرَ السيئ: conjoined to ﴿استكبارًا﴾ or to ﴿نفورًا﴾; السيئ: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and this is an annexation of the qualified noun to its adjective, or the qualified noun is omitted, i.e. "the plotting of the evil deed".
﴿ولا يحيق المكر السيئ إلا بأهله﴾: الواو: circumstantial (ḥāliyya); لا: negating; يحيق: an imperfect verb; المكر: fāʿil (agent); السيئ: naʿt (adjective); إلا: a particle of restriction (adāt ḥaṣr); بأهله: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يحيق﴾; the clause ﴿ولا يحيق...﴾ is circumstantial.
﴿فهل ينظرون إلا سنت الأولين﴾: الفاء: conjunctive; هل: an interrogative particle; ينظرون: an imperfect verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; إلا: a particle of restriction; سنة: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الأولين: muḍāf ilayhi; the interrogative clause is conjoined to the clause ﴿فلما جاءهم نذير...﴾.
﴿فلن تجد لسنت الله تبديلا﴾: الفاء: of faṣīḥa, i.e. "whatever may be, you will not find any change in the way of Allah"; لن: a particle of negation, of the subjunctive and of the future; تجد: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by lan; لسنة: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تبديلا﴾, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi; تبديلا: the object of تجد.
﴿ولن تجد لسنت الله تحويلا﴾: لن: a particle of negation, of the subjunctive and of the future; تجد: an imperfect verb, accusative by lan; لسنة: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تحويلا﴾, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi; تحويلا: the object of تجد; the clause ﴿لن تجد لسنة الله تحويلا﴾ is conjoined to the one before it, ﴿لن تجد لسنة الله تبديلا﴾.

muyesser-irab:44-44.t:
﴿أولم يسيروا في الأرض﴾: the hamza: for disapproving interrogation (al-istifhām al-inkārī); الواو: conjoining to something implied that the context calls for, i.e. "did they keep to their dwellings and not travel?"; لم: a particle of negation, of conversion (to the past) and of the jussive; يسيروا: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil (agent); في الأرض: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسيروا﴾.
﴿فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم﴾: الفاء: conjunctive, and the clause ﴿ينظروا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿يسيروا﴾; كيف: an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as the fronted khabar (predicate) of kāna; كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) verb; عاقبة: the delayed noun of kāna; الذين: a relative noun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); من قبلهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿الذين﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. The pronoun is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿كيف كان عاقبة...﴾ is in the position of accusative as the object of ينظروا.
﴿وكانوا أشد منهم قوة﴾: الواو: circumstantial; كانوا: the defective ﴿كان﴾, and the wāw of the plural is its noun; أشد: the khabar of kāna; منهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أشد﴾; قوة: tamyīz (specification); the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿وما كان الله ليعجزه من شيء في السماوات ولا في الأرض﴾: الواو: conjunctive or circumstantial; ما: negating; كان: a defective verb, and the wāw of the plural is its noun [Translator's note: so in the source; there is no wāw of the plural here, and the noun of ﴿كان﴾ is evidently the Name of Majesty ﴿الله﴾.]; ﴿ليعجزه﴾: ﴿اللام﴾ is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), and ﴿يعجزه﴾ is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām of denial, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied ﴿أن﴾ and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the lām with its genitive is attached to an omitted khabar of kāna; مِن: a redundant preposition (ḥarf jarr ṣila); شيء: fāʿil, nominative in position and genitive in form by ﴿من﴾; في السماوات: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿شيء﴾; ولا في الأرض: conjoined to ﴿في السماوات﴾.
﴿إنه كان عليما قديرا﴾: إنه: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) and the hāʾ is its noun; كان: a defective verb, the noun of kāna latent (mustatir), implied as "هو"; عليمًا: the khabar of kāna; قديرًا: a second khabar of ﴿كان﴾; the clause ﴿كان عليما قديرا﴾ is the khabar of inna, and the clause ﴿إنه كان عليما قديرا﴾ gives the reason for the denial that anything can frustrate Him.

muyesser-irab:45-45.t:
﴿ولو يؤاخذ الله الناس بما كسبوا ما ترك على ظهرها من دابة﴾: الواو: resumptive; لو: conditional; يؤاخذ: an imperfect verb; الله: fāʿil (agent); الناس: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بما: the bāʾ is a preposition and ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun in the position of genitive, i.e. "for that which they earned", or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, i.e. "for their earning"; the bāʾ with its genitive is attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يؤاخذ﴾; كسبوا: a past verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿كسبوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿ما ترك﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; ما: negating; ترك: a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), implied as "هو"; على ظهرها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ترك﴾, and the attached pronoun is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); من: a redundant preposition (ḥarf jarr ṣila); دابة: genitive in form, accusative in position as the object of ترك; the clause ﴿ولو يؤاخذ الله...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿ولكن يؤخرهم إلى أجل مسمى﴾: الواو: conjunctive; لكن: lightened (mukhaffafa) and inoperative (muhmala), for rectification (istidrāk); يؤخرهم: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, implied as "هو", the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi and the mīm is the sign of the plural; إلى أجل: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يؤخرهم﴾; مسمى: naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أجل﴾; the clause ﴿ولكن يؤخرهم...﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿ولو يؤاخذ...﴾.
﴿فإذا جاء أجلهم فإن الله كان بعباده بصيرا﴾: الفاء: conjunctive; إذا: an adverb of the future containing the sense of a condition; جاء: a past verb; أجلهم: fāʿil, and the attached pronoun is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿جاء أجلهم﴾ is in the position of genitive through the adverb being annexed to it; the apodosis (jawāb) of إذا is omitted, its implied form being "يجازيهم بما كسبوا" (He will recompense them for what they earned), and the conditional sentence is conjoined to the clause ﴿يؤخرهم﴾. ﴿فإن﴾: the fāʾ is linking, and ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); the Name of Majesty is the noun of inna; كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) verb, the noun of kāna latent, implied as "هو", referring to Allah the Exalted; بعباده: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿بصيرًا﴾; بصيرًا: the khabar (predicate) of kāna; the clause ﴿كان بعباده بصيرا﴾ is the khabar of inna, and the clause ﴿إن الله كان بعباده بصيرا﴾ gives the reason for the implied apodosis.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿الحمد لله فاطر السماوات والأرض﴾: الحمد: mubtadaʾ (subject); ولله: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; وفاطر: an adjective (ṣifa); والسماوات: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); والأرض: conjoined to السماوات.
﴿جاعل الملائكة رسلا أولي أجنحة مثنى وثلاث ورباع﴾: جاعل: a second adjective; والملائكة: muḍāf ilayhi; ورسلا: the second object of ﴿جاعل﴾, or an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara, circumstantial) if جاعل means "creator"; وأولي: an adjective (naʿt) of ﴿رسلا﴾; وأجنحة: muḍāf ilayhi; ومثنى: an adjective of أجنحة; وثلاث ورباع: conjoined to مثنى.
﴿يزيد في الخلق ما يشاء﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position, and it confirms what precedes it. ويزيد: an imperfect verb; وفي الخلق: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يزيد﴾; وما: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause ﴿يشاء﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿إن الله على كل شيء قدير﴾: إن: an abrogating particle; the Divine Name is the noun of إن; وعلى كل: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿قدير﴾; وشيء: muḍāf ilayhi; وقدير: the khabar of إن; and the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿ما يفتح الله للناس من رحمة فلا ممسك لها﴾: ما: a jussivising conditional noun in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿يفتح﴾; ويفتح: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm) with sukūn, its end being moved with kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; والله: fāʿil (agent); وللناس: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يفتح﴾; ومن رحمة: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the conditional noun; والفاء: linking the apodosis of the condition; ولا: the lā of generic negation; وممسك: the noun of لا; ولها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of لا; and the clause ﴿لا ممسك لها﴾ is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
﴿وما يمسك فلا مرسل له من بعده﴾: الواو: a conjunction; وما: a jussivising conditional noun in the position of accusative as a fronted object of ﴿يمسك﴾; ويمسك: the protasis, jussive; والفاء: linking the apodosis of the condition; ولا: the lā of generic negation; ومرسل: the noun of لا; وله: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of لا; ومن بعده: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what the khabar is attached to, by an omitted ḥāl of the pronoun concealed in the implied khabar of لا. [Translator's note: the Arabic phrase here («متعلقان بما تعلق به خبر بمحذوف حال من الضمير المستكن في خبر لا المقدر») appears garbled in the source, apparently conflating two alternatives: attachment to what the khabar is attached to, or to an omitted ḥāl of the pronoun latent in the implied khabar of لا.]
﴿وهو العزيز الحكيم﴾: الواو: resumptive; وهو: mubtadaʾ (subject); والعزيز: first khabar; والحكيم: second khabar; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: (الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ فاطِرِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): there are three ways in it: the genitive as a naʿt (adjective); the nominative on the implication of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); or the accusative as praise. Sībawayh reported «الحمد لله أهلَ الحمد», which is like it. Likewise (جاعِلِ الْمَلائِكَةِ رُسُلًا); tanwīn is not permissible in it because it refers to the past. (رُسُلًا) is a second object; and it is said: on the implication of a «فاعل», because a «فاعل» (active participle) referring to the past, when it is in a genitive construct, does not govern anything. [Translator's note: «على إضمار فاعل» is as written; the sense appears to be that «رسلاً» is governed by an implied verb, since the participle in the past sense cannot govern.] (أُولِي أَجْنِحَةٍ) is a naʿt; Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. possessors of wings. (مَثْنى وَثُلاثَ وَرُباعَ) are diptotes because there are two causes in them: one of them is that they are deflected forms (maʿdūla), and this is agreed upon; there is disagreement about the second, because the early grammarians did not mention it. Abū Isḥāq said: the second cause is that it was deflected while indefinite. Others said: the second cause is that it is an adjective. A third view is that it is deflected from «اثنين اثنين» ("two by two"), and that is a second cause.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: The grammarians permitted outside the Qurʾān: «فلا ممسك له» (then there is none to withhold it — masculine), according to the wording of «ما», while «لها» (feminine) is according to the meaning. They permitted: (وَما يُمْسِكْ) «فلا مرسل لها», according to the meaning of «ما». And they permitted «فلا ممسكٌ لها» [in the nominative], in the sense of «ليس», and likewise «فلا مرسلٌ له». And they permitted «ما يفتحُ الله للناس من رحمة», with «ما» in the sense of «الذي» (that which).

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
﴿يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ هَلْ مِنْ خالِقٍ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَرْزُقُكُمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ لا إِلهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ فَأَنَّى تُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ (3)

(يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ هَلْ مِنْ خالِقٍ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ): this is the reading of Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim. Shaqīq ibn Salama, Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «هل من خالق غيرِ الله». [Translator's note: the source prints this second reading without vowels; the genitive «غيرِ» is the reading of Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī, as the following "the genitive according to the wording" indicates.] It is permissible to put «غير» in the accusative as an exception. The nominative is from two angles: one of them in the sense of "Is there any creator except Allah?", meaning "There is no creator except Allah"; the second way is that it is a naʿt (adjective) on the position, because the meaning is "Is there a creator other than Allah?". The genitive is according to the wording. Ḥammād ibn Salama said: Ḥumayd al-Ṭawīl told us: I said to al-Ḥasan: "Who created evil?" He said: "Glory be to Allah! Is there any creator other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic? Allah created good and evil."

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: (وَإِنْ يُكَذِّبُوكَ فَقَدْ كُذِّبَتْ رُسُلٌ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ): as a consolation for him ﷺ. (وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُ): Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. the return of matters is to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and He will recompense whoever gave the lie and give victory to those of His messengers who were given the lie.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: (يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ فَلا تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا): Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: the delusion of the life of this world is that a person is distracted by its pleasures and its trials from working for the Hereafter, until (يَقُولُ يا لَيْتَنِي قَدَّمْتُ لِحَياتِي) [al-Fajr: 24]. (وَلا يَغُرَّنَّكُمْ بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ): Shuʿba reported from Simāk (وَلا يَغُرَّنَّكُمْ بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ) with ḍamma on the ghayn [«الغُرور»]. There are three views on it. Among them: that it is the plural of «غارّ» (deceiver), as you say «جالس» and «جلوس»; this is the best of what has been said about it, and its meaning is then like the meaning of «الغَرور» (the Deceiver). [Translator's note: the source reads «مع غار», evidently for «جمع غارّ» "plural of غارّ".] Abū Ḥātim said: «الغُرور» is the plural of «غَرّ», and «غَرّ» is a maṣdar (verbal noun). The third view is that «الغُرور» is a maṣdar; this is far-fetched according to Abū Isḥāq, because «غررته» is transitive, and the maṣdar of a transitive verb is only on the pattern «فَعْل», as in «ضربته ضرباً», except for a few things that were heard and on which no analogy is built: they said «لزمته لزوماً» and «نهكه المرض نهوكاً». [Translator's note: the source prints «لزما», but the example requires the anomalous «لزوماً».] As for the meaning of this word, the best of what has been said about it is what Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: delusion concerning Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is that a person commits sins and then hopes for forgiveness from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: (إِنَّ الشَّيْطانَ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ): «عدوّ» may be in the sense of «معادٍ» (one who shows enmity), and then it takes the dual, the plural and the feminine; or it may be in the sense of attribution, and then it is singular in every case, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: (فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِي) [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 77]; and on this basis the feminine is also «عدوّ». As for the statement of some grammarians that the wāw is weak, so they brought the hāʾ [i.e. «عدوّة»], it is an error; rather, the wāw is a strong letter. (فَاتَّخِذُوهُ عَدُوًّا): two objects. (إِنَّما يَدْعُوا حِزْبَهُ): «ما» has restrained «إنّ» from governing, so the verb came after it. (لِيَكُونُوا مِنْ أَصْحابِ السَّعِيرِ).

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: (الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) may be a badal (substitute) for «أصحاب», and then it is in the position of the genitive; it may be a badal for «حزبه», and then it is in the position of the accusative; or it may be a badal for the wāw [in «ليكونوا»], and then it is in the position of the nominative. A fourth view, and it is the best of them: it is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is (لَهُمْ عَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ). As for (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا), it is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is (لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ).

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: (أَفَمَنْ زُيِّنَ لَهُ سُوءُ عَمَلِهِ): «مَن» is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is omitted because of what indicates it. Al-Kisāʾī said: and what indicates it is (فَلا تَذْهَبْ نَفْسُكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَسَراتٍ), the meaning being: "Is the one to whom the evil of his deed has been made fair-seeming, so that he sees it as good — [for such] has your soul gone out in sorrows over them?" He said: this is good, elegant Arabic speech which few know. What al-Kisāʾī said is the best of what has been said about the verse, because of the indication of the omitted part which he mentioned. [Translator's note: the source reads «لما ذكره فمن الدلالة», evidently for «لما ذكره من الدلالة».] The meaning is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbade the Prophet ﷺ from intense distress over them and grief for them, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: (لَعَلَّكَ باخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ) [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 3]; the people of tafsīr said: i.e. killing yourself. It was read to Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā from Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq, who said: Naṣr ibn ʿAlī told us: I asked al-Aṣmaʿī about the saying of the Prophet ﷺ concerning the people of Yemen, "They are the softest of hearts and the most «أبخع» in obedience" — what does "أبخع طاعة" mean? He said: the most sincere in obedience. I said to him: "The people of tafsīr, Mujāhid and others, say about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, (لَعَلَّكَ باخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ) that its meaning is 'killing yourself'." He said: "It is from exactly that; it is as though, from the intensity of his sincerity towards them, he were killing himself." The reading of Abū Jaʿfar is «فلا تُذْهِبْ نفسَك» [Translator's note: the source prints this reading with the same vowelling as the standard one, (فَلا تَذْهَبْ نَفْسُكَ); the transitive form given here is the known reading of Abū Jaʿfar], and the two meanings are close. «حسرات» is accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) or as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: (مَنْ كانَ يُرِيدُ الْعِزَّةَ): the implied form according to al-Farrāʾ is "whoever desires knowledge of might". Likewise others among the people of knowledge said: whoever desires knowledge of the might with which there is no abasement — because when might leads to abasement, it is itself exposed to abasement, and the might with which there is no abasement belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. (جَمِيعاً) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Isḥāq rendered its meaning: whoever desires, by worshipping Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to be mighty through it — Allah will make him mighty in the Hereafter and in this world. (إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ): the statement is complete. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read «إليه يصعد الكلامُ». «الكلم» is the plural of «كلمة». The people of tafsīr — Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, Shahr ibn Ḥawshab and others — said: the meaning is that righteous action raises the good word. This is a refutation of the Murjiʾa. (وَالْعَمَلُ الصَّالِحُ) is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), or on the implication of a verb. As for its being nominative in the sense of "and righteous action raises it", that is an error, because when the agent precedes the verb it is not made nominative by the verb. This is the view of all the grammarians, except something that ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān related to us from Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, that he permitted «زيد قام» in the sense of «قام زيد». Abū Jaʿfar said: what shows you the unsoundness of this is the Arabs' saying «الزيدان قاما»; were it as he said, it would be said «الزيدان قام». (وَالَّذِينَ يَمْكُرُونَ السَّيِّئاتِ) in the sense of "those who do evil deeds", so «السيئات» is an object; and it is possible that the implied form is "those who do evil", so «السيئات» is a maṣdar (verbal noun). (لَهُمْ عَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ) is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين». (وَمَكْرُ أُولئِكَ) is a mubtadaʾ, and «هو» is a second mubtadaʾ, and (يَبُورُ) is the khabar of the second; it may also be a khabar of the first, with «هو» redundant (zāʾida). [Translator's note: the source reads «هذا زائدة», evidently for «هو زائدة».] One says «بار يبور» when something perishes; from it is «بارت السوق» (the market became stagnant), and "we seek refuge in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from the stagnation (bawār) of the unmarried woman".

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: (وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ تُرابٍ): Saʿīd reported from Qatāda; he said: meaning Ādam ﷺ, and the implied form on this basis is "He created your origin from dust". (ثُمَّ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ): he said: i.e. that which He brought forth from the loins of your fathers. (ثُمَّ جَعَلَكُمْ أَزْواجاً): he said: i.e. He paired some of you with others. (وَما يُعَمَّرُ مِنْ مُعَمَّرٍ وَلا يُنْقَصُ مِنْ عُمُرِهِ إِلَّا فِي كِتابٍ): ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn told us from al-Ḥasan ibn Ḥamd, who said: Ibn ʿAwāna told us from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: "No one is granted long life except that his lifespan is written: how many years is it? how many months? how many days? and how many hours? Then it is written at his lifespan: so much has decreased, so much has decreased, until the decrease matches the lifespan." The position of al-Farrāʾ on the meaning of (وَما يُعَمَّرُ مِنْ مُعَمَّرٍ) is: none has his life lengthened, and none has [his] life shortened — meaning another — i.e. nor is the other's life decreased from the life of that one, (إِلَّا فِي كِتابٍ). (إِنَّ ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ): its verb is «يسر»; and were you to name a person with it, it would be fully declined, because it is on the pattern «فعيل».

nahhas-irab:12-13.t:
(وَما يَسْتَوِي الْبَحْرانِ هذا عَذْبٌ فُراتٌ): it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: «فرات» is sweet, and «أجاج» is salty and bitter. Ṭalḥa read «وهذا مَلِحٌ أجاج» with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the lām, without alif. As for «المالح», it is one who puts salt in something to improve it. (وَمِنْ كُلٍّ تَأْكُلُونَ لَحْماً طَرِيًّا): there is no disagreement that this is from both of them together. (وَتَسْتَخْرِجُونَ حِلْيَةً تَلْبَسُونَها): the position of Abū Isḥāq is that the ornaments are only extracted from the salt [water], and it was said "from both" because they are mixed. Others said: the shells, about which it says "ornaments", of pearls and others, are only extracted from places where there is both sweet and salt, such as springs. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd held a third view, which is the best of them; he said: the ornaments are extracted from the salt [water] specifically, and in his view this is not because they are mixed; rather, the two were joined together and then a statement was made about one of them, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: (وَمِنْ رَحْمَتِهِ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ لِتَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ وَلِتَبْتَغُوا مِنْ فَضْلِهِ) [Yūnus: 67] [Translator's note: this wording is in al-Qaṣaṣ: 73; Yūnus: 67 has a different wording], and as you say: "Had you seen al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥajjāj, you would have seen good and evil," and as you say: "Had you seen al-Aṣmaʿī and Sībawayh, you would have filled your hand with lexicon and grammar"; the meaning of this is known, and it is frequent, eloquent speech. So it is here: (وَمِنْ كُلٍّ تَأْكُلُونَ لَحْماً طَرِيًّا وَتَسْتَخْرِجُونَ حِلْيَةً تَلْبَسُونَها) — they are together in the first, and the salt is alone in the second, so they become together in all of this. He said: (وَتَرَى الْفُلْكَ فِيهِ مَواخِرَ), i.e. in the salt [water] specifically; were it not so, He would have said «فيهما» (in both). «مخرت السفينة تمخَر وتمخُر» is said when the ship cleaves the water, as Ṭarafa said: [al-Ṭawīl] 354-
يشقّ حباب الماء حيزومها بها ... كما قسم التّرب المفايل باليد
(Its breast cleaves the bubbles of the water with it, as the player of al-fiyāl divides the earth with his hand.)
And it was said: the appointed term here is the Resurrection, because with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, it is appointed for a known time. (وَالَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ ما يَمْلِكُونَ مِنْ قِطْمِيرٍ): ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: «القطمير» is the skin of the date-stone.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: (إِنْ تَدْعُوهُمْ لا يَسْمَعُوا دُعاءَكُمْ): a condition and its apodosis. (وَلَوْ سَمِعُوا مَا اسْتَجابُوا لَكُمْ): it has the meaning of the first, even though «لو» is not used to give a conditional apodosis [in the jussive]. [Translator's note: the source reads «وإن كانت لولا يجازى بها», evidently «وإن كانت لو لا يجازى بها».] Qatāda said: (مَا اسْتَجابُوا لَكُمْ) — they would not follow you nor accept from you. (وَيَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ يَكْفُرُونَ بِشِرْكِكُمْ): Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. they will say, "It was not us they worshipped." (وَلا يُنَبِّئُكَ مِثْلُ خَبِيرٍ): Qatāda said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed that this will happen from you on the Day of Resurrection.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: (يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ أَنْتُمُ الْفُقَراءُ إِلَى اللَّهِ): lightening the second hamza is the best of the ways according to al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him; it is also permissible to lighten the first, to drop it, to lighten both together, and to pronounce both fully. (وَاللَّهُ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ): «هو» may be redundant (zāʾida), having no position in iʿrāb, or it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), so that its position is nominative.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: (إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ): a condition and its apodosis, and there is an omission in it which the Arabs use frequently; the implied form is "If He wills to remove you, He will remove you". From «يشأ» the ḍamma that was on the hamza was dropped, and when it became quiescent, the alif before it was dropped. (وَيَأْتِ) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «يذهبكم».

nahhas-irab:9-9.t:
(بَلَدٍ مَيِّتٍ): «مَيْت» and «مَيِّت» are one [in meaning], and likewise «مَيْتة» and «مَيِّتة» are one. This is the view of the skilled grammarians. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: this is the view of the Basrans, and he made no exception of anyone, and he adduced decisive proofs for it from the speech of the Arabs. He recited: [al-Khafīf] 352-
ليس من مات فاستراح بميت ... إنّما الميت ميّت الأحياء
إنّما الميت من يعيش كئيبا ... كاسفا باله قليل الرّخاء
(Not he who died and found rest is dead; the dead is only the dead among the living. The dead is only he who lives in gloom, downcast in mind, with little ease.)
It is also transmitted as «قليل الرّجاء» (with little hope). He said: do you see any difference between «مَيْت» and «مَيِّت»? And he recited: [al-Basīṭ] 353-
هينون لينون أيسار بنو يسر ... سوّاس مكرمة أبناء أيسار
(Gentle, mild, generous players at the lots, sons of generosity, managers of noble deeds, sons of generous men.)
He said: they have agreed that his saying «هَيْنون» and «هَيِّنون» are one, and likewise «مَيْت» and «مَيِّت», and «سَيْد» and «سَيِّد». He said: Sībawayh claimed that their «كان كينونة» and «صار صيرورة» are originally «كيّنونة» and «صيّرورة», and likewise «قيدودة». Muḥammad ibn Yazīd refuted the Kufans' statement that it is on the pattern «فَعْلول» from two angles: one, that there is no «فَعْلول» in the speech of the Arabs; and the second, that had it been as they said, it would have been with wāw. [Translator's note: the doubled forms «كيّنونة», «صيّرونة» are implied by the argument; the source writes both forms identically without shadda.] Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a clear, good argument regarding «كينونة», because it is from «الكون», and regarding «القيدودة», because it is from «الأقود». (كَذلِكَ النُّشُورُ), i.e. thus will you be brought to life after you have died; from «نشر الإنسان نشوراً» when he comes to life, and «أنشره الله» (Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revived him).

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: (وَلا تَزِرُ) is cut off from what precedes it. The original is «تَوْزِر»; the wāw was dropped in conformity with «يَزِر». (وازِرَةٌ) is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted noun, i.e. "a burdened soul"; and likewise (وَإِنْ تَدْعُ مُثْقَلَةٌ): al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. a heavily laden soul or beast; he said: this applies to the masculine and the feminine. Al-Akhfash said: i.e. "and if a heavily laden one calls a person (إِلى حِمْلِها)". «الحِمْل» is what is on the back; «حَمْل» of a woman and «حَمْل» of a palm-tree al-Kisāʾī reported with fatḥa only, while Ibn al-Sikkīt reported that «حمل» of a palm-tree takes fatḥa and kasra. (وَلَوْ كانَ ذا قُرْبى): the implied form according to al-Akhfash's view is "even if the person called were a near relative". Al-Farrāʾ permitted «ولو كان ذو قربى». Abū Jaʿfar said: this is permissible according to Sībawayh, and like it is (وَإِنْ كانَ ذُو عُسْرَةٍ) [al-Baqara: 280]; «كان» is then in the sense of "occurred", or the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "if among those from whom you demand there is one in difficulty". Sībawayh reported: «الناس مجزيّون بأعمالهم إن خيرٌ فخيرٌ» ("people are recompensed for their deeds: if good, then good") on this [pattern], and «إن خيراً فخيراً» on the first. Al-Ḥakam ibn Abān reported from ʿIkrima that he said: "It has reached me that the Jew and the Christian will see the Muslim man on the Day of Resurrection and say to him: 'Did I not do you a favour? Did I not treat you well?' He will say: 'Yes.' He will say: 'Then benefit me.' And the Muslim will keep decreasing his punishment. And a man will come to his father on the Day of Resurrection and say: 'Was I not dutiful to you, compassionate towards you and good to you? You see the state I am in; so give me one of your good deeds, or bear one evil deed for me.' He will say: 'What you have asked of me is small, but I fear what you fear.' And the father will say the like of that to his son, and he will answer him with something similar. And a man will say to his wife: 'Was I not of good companionship to you? Then bear a sin for me; perhaps I will be saved.' She will say: 'That is small, but I fear what you fear.'" Then ʿIkrima recited: (وَإِنْ تَدْعُ مُثْقَلَةٌ إِلى حِمْلِها لا يُحْمَلْ مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ وَلَوْ كانَ ذا قُرْبى). (إِنَّما تُنْذِرُ الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ): he warns all creatures, but He singled out those who fear their Lord because they are the ones who benefit from the warning.

nahhas-irab:19-21.t:
﴿وَما يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمى وَالْبَصِيرُ﴾ (19) ﴿وَلا الظُّلُماتُ وَلا النُّورُ﴾ (20) ﴿وَلا الظِّلُّ وَلا الْحَرُورُ﴾ (21)

(وَما يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمى وَالْبَصِيرُ): it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: the believer and the disbeliever. He said: (الظُّلُماتُ) is misguidance, (النُّورُ) is guidance, (الظِّلُّ) is Paradise, and (الْحَرُورُ) is the Fire. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: «لا» is redundant (zāʾida), and the meaning is "nor the darknesses and the light, nor the shade and the hot wind". It was said: «الحرور» is only by night, and «السموم» is by day; and it was said: «الحرور» is in both. This is the sounder of the two views, because «حرور» is «فعول» from «الحرّ» (heat), and there is in it the meaning of intensity, i.e. harmful heat.
Al-Ḥasan read «وما أنت بمسمعِ من في القبور», the tanwīn being dropped for lightness; i.e. they are like the people of the graves in that they do not benefit from what they hear nor accept it. [Translator's note: the source prints this reading with the standard vowelling (وَما أَنْتَ بِمُسْمِعٍ مَنْ فِي الْقُبُورِ); the comment shows that al-Ḥasan's reading is without tanwīn, in genitive construct. The source also has «أهل القبول», evidently for «أهل القبور» "the people of the graves".]

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: (بِالْبَيِّناتِ وَبِالزُّبُرِ): and in another place (الزُّبُرِ) [Āl ʿImrān: 184] without bāʾ, and the meaning is the same, except that what is frequent in the speech of the Arabs is without bāʾ, and with what follows also with bāʾ; so the bāʾ, when it enters, is tawkīd (emphasis), or it is the conjoining of a clause to a clause with the verb omitted because the first indicates it.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: You put (مُخْتَلِفاً) in the accusative because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «ثمرات», and (أَلْوانُها) is nominative by «مختلف»; it is fit to be a naʿt of «ثمرات» because of the pronoun referring back to it. Its nominative is permissible outside the Qurʾān. Like it: «رأيت رجلاً خارجاً أبوه» ("I saw a man whose father was going out"). (وَمِنَ الْجِبالِ جُدَدٌ): plural of «جُدّة» (streak). Al-Akhfash said: had it been the plural of «جديد», it would have been said «جُدُد», like «رغيف» and «رُغُف». (بِيضٌ وَحُمْرٌ مُخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوانُها): «مختلف» is nominative here and accusative there, because what precedes it here is nominative, so it is a naʿt of it; and it may be nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: It is said here (أَلْوانُهُ) and there «أَلْوانُها», because its implied form is "and a creation differing in its colours"; and «مختلف» is a naʿt (adjective) put in the place of the qualified noun. The kāf [of «كذلك»] is in the position of a naʿt, because it is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun). (إِنَّما يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبادِهِ الْعُلَماءُ): Mujāhid said: the learned one is only he who fears Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him: "Fear of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, suffices as knowledge, and being deluded about Him suffices as ignorance."

nahhas-irab:29-29.t:
﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَتْلُونَ كِتابَ اللَّهِ وَأَقامُوا الصَّلاةَ وَأَنْفَقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقْناهُمْ سِرًّا وَعَلانِيَةً يَرْجُونَ تِجارَةً لَنْ تَبُورَ﴾ (29)

(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَتْلُونَ كِتابَ اللَّهِ): Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ» is (يَرْجُونَ تِجارَةً لَنْ تَبُورَ).

nahhas-irab:32-33.t: (ثُمَّ أَوْرَثْنَا الْكِتابَ الَّذِينَ اصْطَفَيْنا مِنْ عِبادِنا): this verse is difficult, because He, Mighty and Majestic, said (اصْطَفَيْنا مِنْ عِبادِنا) and then He, Mighty and Majestic, said (فَمِنْهُمْ ظالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ). We had mentioned it before, but we will explain it here with the utmost clarity. A number of the Companions, the Followers and those after them have spoken about it. Among the soundest of what has been reported on that is what was read to Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Imām, from Yūsuf ibn Mūsā, from Wakīʿ ibn al-Jarrāḥ, who said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna told us from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: «فَمِنْهُمْ ظالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ» — he said: the disbeliever. And it was read to Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Ḥabīb, from al-Faḍl ibn Mūsā, from Ḥusayn, from Yazīd, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: (ثُمَّ أَوْرَثْنَا الْكِتابَ الَّذِينَ اصْطَفَيْنا مِنْ عِبادِنا فَمِنْهُمْ ظالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ وَمِنْهُمْ مُقْتَصِدٌ وَمِنْهُمْ سابِقٌ بِالْخَيْراتِ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ) — he said: two groups were saved. This is one view; and the implied form in Arabic is then «فمنهم», i.e. "of Our servants", «ظالم لنفسه», i.e. a disbeliever. Al-Ḥasan said: i.e. a sinner (fāsiq). And the pronoun in «يدخلونها» then refers back to the moderate one and the foremost one, not to the wrongdoer. As for the meaning of «الذين اصطفينا من عبادنا», there are two views on it: one is that those chosen are the prophets, Allah's blessings be upon them, i.e. they were chosen for the message; and it was said: the meaning is those chosen for the Book to be sent down to them, and this is general. And it was said: the pronoun in (يَدْخُلُونَها) refers back to all three classes, on the basis that the wrongdoer here is neither a disbeliever nor a sinner. Among those from whom this view is reported — I mean that those who enter it are these three classes — are ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, Abū al-Dardāʾ, Ibn Masʿūd, ʿUqba ibn ʿAmr and ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with them. Were it not for our dislike of length, we would have mentioned that with its chains of transmission, though they are not like the first chains in soundness. This view is also soundly transmitted from ʿUbayd ibn ʿAmr, Kaʿb al-Aḥbār and others among the Followers. The interpretation according to this view is that the one who wrongs himself is the one who committed minor sins; and the moderate one — Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: he is the one who gives this world its due and the Hereafter its due. So «جنّات عدن يدخلونها» refers back to all of them, according to this explanation and clarification. There is a third view on the verse: «الظالم» is the one who commits major sins, and the moderate one is he who has not merited Paradise by his good deeds exceeding his evil deeds; so «جنّات عدن يدخلونها» refers to those who are foremost in good deeds and no others. [Translator's note: the source reads «الذين سبقونا بالخيرات», evidently for «الذين سبقوا بالخيرات».] This is the view of a group of the people of reasoning; they said: because the pronoun, in strict reasoning, more fittingly belongs to what is next to it. We have mentioned the view of the earlier scholars before this. (يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيها مِنْ أَساوِرَ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ): plural of «أسورة», and «أسورة» is the plural of «سِوار» and «سُوار». It has been reported that one says «إسوار», and the plural of «إسوار» is «أساوير»; it has been reported that in the codex (ḥarf) of Ubayy is «أساوير». Dropping the yāʾ from [the pattern] «مفاعيل» in this is permissible; but what is known is that «الأسوار» is the man who is a good archer among the Persians. (وَلُؤْلُؤاً) [in the accusative] is the reading of the people of Medina. Abū Isḥāq said: because the meaning of «من أساور» and the meaning of «أساور» are one. The genitive is the reading of the people of Kufa, and it is clearer in Arabic, because it is a genitive conjoined to a genitive. ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read «جنّاتِ عدن يدخلونها» with kasra on the tāʾ, which is then in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) for «الخيرات»; and it may be in the position of the accusative according to the dialect of those who say «زيداً ضربته». [Translator's note: the source prints this reading with the standard vowelling (جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَها).] Some of the people of reasoning claimed that His words, Mighty and Majestic, (يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيها مِنْ أَساوِرَ) are about the women, because His words, Mighty and Majestic, (مِنْ عِبادِنا) include males and females. This is a clear error, because had it been about the women it would have been «يُحَلَّيْن»; rather it is about the men only — though women may be adorned with it, and when women are adorned with it, it is for their husbands.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: (وَقالُوا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الْحَزَنَ): from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: the Fire. Saʿīd reported from Qatāda; he said: they used to work in this world and toil, and grief would afflict them. Shamir ibn ʿAṭiyya said about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, (وَقالُوا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الْحَزَنَ): he said: the worry over food. He said: (إِنَّ رَبَّنا لَغَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ): He forgave them the sins they committed, and appreciated for them the good to which He guided them and which they did.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: (الَّذِي أَحَلَّنا دارَ الْمُقامَةِ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ): «الذي» may be in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of the noun of «إنّ»; it may be in the position of the nominative on the implication of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or as a khabar (predicate) after the khabar of «إنّ», or as a badal (substitute) for «غفور», or as a badal for the latent pronoun in «شكور»; and it may be in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: (الْمُقامَةِ) [with ḍamma] is residence, and «المَقامة» [with fatḥa] is the assembly in which one stands. [Translator's note: the source reads «الإمامة», evidently for «الإقامة» "residence".] (لا يَمَسُّنا فِيها نَصَبٌ), i.e. fatigue. «النُّصْب» is evil, and «النُّصُب» is what is set up for slaughter or otherwise. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read «ولا يمسّنا فيها لَغوب» with fatḥa on the lām [the source prints (وَلا يَمَسُّنا فِيها لُغُوبٌ)]; it is then a maṣdar (verbal noun), like «الوَقود» and «الطَّهور»; and it was said: it is that from which one becomes weary.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is (لَهُمْ نارُ جَهَنَّمَ); the khabar may also be (لا يُقْضى عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَمُوتُوا). The nūn was dropped because it is the answer to a negation. Al-Ḥasan read «لا يقضى عليهم فيموتون» by conjunction. Al-Kisāʾī said: (وَلا يُؤْذَنُ لَهُمْ فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ) [al-Mursalāt: 36] is with nūn in the muṣḥaf because it is the end of a verse, and (لا يُقْضى عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَمُوتُوا) is without nūn because it is not the end of a verse; and in each of them what is permissible in the other is permissible.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: (وَهُمْ يَصْطَرِخُونَ فِيها): the ṭāʾ is substituted for a tāʾ, because ṭāʾ is more like ṣād, both being velarized (muṭbaq) letters. One says «اصطرخ» when one cries for help. (رَبَّنا أَخْرِجْنا), i.e. they say. (نَعْمَلْ صالِحاً) is the answer to the request, i.e. if You bring us out we will do righteousness other than what we used to do. (أَوَلَمْ نُعَمِّرْكُمْ), i.e. then it will be said to them. Abū Hurayra reported from the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever is given life to sixty years, Allah has left him no excuse in [length of] life." Likewise Sahl ibn Saʿd reported from the Prophet ﷺ something of similar meaning. Ibn ʿAbbās said about His words, Mighty and Majestic, (أَوَلَمْ نُعَمِّرْكُمْ ما يَتَذَكَّرُ فِيهِ مَنْ تَذَكَّرَ): he said: sixty years. (وَجاءَكُمُ النَّذِيرُ), i.e. the warner; and in [the pattern] «فعيل» there is the meaning of intensity. It was said: by it is meant the Prophet ﷺ; and it was said: it is whoever warned them; and it was said: by it is meant grey hair; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows best.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: When it is without tanwīn, it is fit for the past, the future and the present; and when it has tanwīn, it may not be for the past.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: (هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَكُمْ خَلائِفَ فِي الْأَرْضِ): plural of «خليفة», i.e. you succeed those who were before you. In this there is the meaning of warning and taking heed, i.e. so beware lest punishment descend on you as it descended on those before you. (فَمَنْ كَفَرَ فَعَلَيْهِ كُفْرُهُ) is like (وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ) [Yūsuf: 82], i.e. the punishment of his disbelief. (وَلا يَزِيدُ الْكافِرِينَ كُفْرُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَّا مَقْتاً): two objects; and likewise (وَلا يَزِيدُ الْكافِرِينَ كُفْرُهُمْ إِلَّا خَساراً).

nahhas-irab:40-40.t:
(قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ شُرَكاءَكُمُ) is accusative by [the verb of] seeing, and its nominative is not permissible. The nominative may be permissible according to Sībawayh in their saying «قد علمتُ زيدٌ أبو من هو» ("I know Zayd — whose father he is"), because Zayd is, in meaning, the one asked about; but if you said «أرأيتَ زيداً أبو من هو؟», the nominative would not be permissible. The difference between them is that the meaning of this is "inform me about him"; and likewise the meaning of this [verse] is: inform me about your partners whom you call upon besides Allah — did you worship them because they have a share in the creation of the heavens, or did they create anything of the earth, or did We give them a Book with this? I.e. or do they have a Book which We sent down to them with partnership, or [stating] that We commanded them to worship them? So in this is a refutation of everyone who worships other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because they do not find in any of the Books that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded that other than Him be worshipped.
«على بيّنات منه» is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī; Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read (عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِنْهُ). Abū Jaʿfar said: the two meanings are close, except that the reading «بيّنات» is preferable, because whoever read «على بيّنة» must either have differed from the main body of the text [of the muṣḥaf], or have brought it according to the dialect of those who say «جاءني طلحة», pausing with tāʾ [i.e. «طلحت» rather than «طلحه»]; and this is an anomalous, rare dialect.
(بَلْ إِنْ يَعِدُ الظَّالِمُونَ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضاً): «إن» is in the sense of «ما» (not), and that is why you made the verb nominative. (بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضاً): «بعضهم» [is a badal (substitute) for «الظالمون»]. [Translator's note: the source breaks off after «بعضهم»; the bracketed completion is added.] (إِلَّا غُرُوراً), i.e. except delusion with falsehood.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُمْسِكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ أَنْ تَزُولا): «أن» is in the position of the accusative in the sense of "disliking [that]", or it is construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is "Allah prevents the heavens and the earth from ceasing". (وَلَئِنْ زالَتا إِنْ أَمْسَكَهُما مِنْ أَحَدٍ): al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. "and were they to cease, none would hold them after Him", and «إن» is in the sense of «ما». [Translator's note: the source prints «أان», a misprint for «إن».] He said: it is like His words, the Exalted: (وَلَئِنْ أَرْسَلْنا رِيحاً فَرَأَوْهُ مُصْفَرًّا لَظَلُّوا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ يَكْفُرُونَ) [al-Rūm: 51].

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: (وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ): Abū Isḥāq said: they had sworn and exerted themselves [in swearing]. Abū Jaʿfar said: the oath falls on (لَيَكُونُنَّ أَهْدى مِنْ إِحْدَى الْأُمَمِ). Al-Akhfash said: «إحدى» was made feminine because «أمّة» is feminine. (فَلَمَّا جاءَهُمْ نَذِيرٌ ما زادَهُمْ إِلَّا نُفُوراً), i.e. from the truth.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t:
(اسْتِكْباراً) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. out of arrogance towards the truth. (وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to it. Saʿīd reported from Qatāda: i.e. and the plotting of polytheism. Abū Jaʿfar said: the root meaning of evil plotting in the language is lying and deception with falsehood. Al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read «ومكرَ السّيّئْ ولا يحيق المكر السيّئُ إلا بأهله», dropping the case ending from the first and keeping it in the second. [Translator's note: the source prints the reading without vowels and with «ولا يحق» for «ولا يحيق»; the sukūn on the first «السيّئ» is supplied from the explanation.] Abū Isḥāq said: it is a solecism (laḥn) which is not permissible. Abū Jaʿfar said: it became a solecism only because the case ending was dropped from it. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd claimed that this is permissible neither in prose nor in poetry, because the case vowels may not be dropped, since they were introduced to distinguish between meanings. Some grammarians considered it too grave that al-Aʿmash, with his eminence and standing, should read this way, and said: he only paused on it, and whoever claimed this from him erred. He said: the proof of this is that it is the end of the statement, and that since the second was not the end of the statement, he gave it its case ending; and the vowel in the second is heavier than in the first, because it is a ḍamma between two kasras. Some grammarians argued for Ḥamza in this with the view of Sībawayh, and that he and others recited: [al-Rajaz] 355-
إذا اعوججن قلت صاحب قوّم ... بالدوّ أمثال السّفين العوّم
(When they swerved, I said: "Companion, straighten [them]" — in the desert, like floating ships.)
And another said: [al-Sarīʿ] 356-
فاليوم أشرب غير مستحقب ... إثما من الله ولا واغل
(So today I drink, not incurring sin before Allah, nor intruding uninvited.)
There is no proof in this, because Sībawayh did not permit it; some grammarians merely reported it. And a report, when it is said to be from some scholar, is no proof — how much less when he only brought it as anomalous and as poetic licence, and he has been contradicted in it. Abū Isḥāq claimed that Abū al-ʿAbbās recited it to him: [al-Rajaz] 357-
إذا اعوججن قلت صاح قوّم
(When they swerved, I said: "O companion, straighten [them].")
and that he recited it «فاليوم فاشرب» with fāʾ. (فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا سُنَّتَ الْأَوَّلِينَ), i.e. they await only the punishment which descended on the earlier disbelievers. (فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَحْوِيلًا), i.e. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the punishment befall the disbelievers and made that a practice (sunna) concerning them; so He punishes with the like of it whoever deserves it, and no one is able to change that or divert it.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: Abū Isḥāq said: (لِيُعْجِزَهُ) — to escape Him …

nahhas-irab:45-45.t:
(وَلَوْ يُؤاخِذُ اللَّهُ النَّاسَ بِما كَسَبُوا) is with hamza, because the Arabs say «أخذتُ فلاناً بكذا وكذا» ("I took so-and-so to account for such-and-such"), and one does not say «وأخذت». But if you lighten the hamza in «يؤاخذ», it is permissible, and you say «يُواخِذ», changing it into a wāw. If someone says: "Why not change it into an alif, when it has fatḥa?", I say: this is impossible, because what precedes alif is never anything but fatḥa. (عَلى ظَهْرِها) refers back to the earth, which has been mentioned before.
(فَإِذا جاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ بِعِبادِهِ بَصِيراً): it is not permissible that the governing word of «إذا» be «بصيراً», just as «اليوم أنّ زيداً خارج» is not permissible; rather, what governs it is «جاء», because it resembles the conditional particles, and it is sometimes used as a conditional, as he said: [al-Ṭawīl] 358-
إذا قصرت أسيافنا كان وصلها ... خطانا إلى أعدائنا فنضارب
(When our swords fall short, their extension is our steps towards our enemies, and so we strike.)

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَمَا يَسْتَوِي ٱلأَحْيَآءُ وَلاَ ٱلأَمْوَاتُ﴾.
That is, those who reason and the ignorant.
What is meant by "the living" (al-aḥyāʾ) is: those whose hearts are alive with faith and knowledge.
And "the dead" (al-amwāt): those whose hearts are dead because unbelief has overcome them, until they no longer distinguish guidance from error.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِن مِّنْ أُمَّةٍ إِلاَّ خَلاَ فِيهَا نَذِيرٌ﴾.
That is, a prophet passed among it before.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ جُدَدٌ بِيضٌ وَحُمْرٌ مُّخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوَانُهَا وَغَرَابِيبُ سُودٌ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, different colours, i.e. white, red and black. He said: and al-judad are the tracks (streaks).
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū ʿUbayda said: al-ghirbīb is the intensely black.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَٱلدَّوَآبِّ وَٱلأَنْعَامِ مُخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوَانُهُ كَذَلِكَ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, and among people there are the white, the red and the black.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَاءُ﴾.
That is, those who know His power over whatever He wills; whoever knows that is certain that He will punish disobedience, and so fears Him.
As ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَاءُ﴾.
He said: those who know that Allah has power over all things.
And in the ḥadīth: (Fear of Allah suffices as knowledge, and being deluded about Him suffices as ignorance).

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ثُمَّ أَوْرَثْنَا ٱلْكِتَابَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱصْطَفَيْنَا مِنْ عِبَادِنَا فَمِنْهُمْ ظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِ وَمِنْهُمْ مُّقْتَصِدٌ وَمِنْهُمْ سَابِقٌ بِٱلْخَيْرَاتِ بِإِذُنِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
It has been said that the one who is saved is the moderate (al-muqtaṣid) and the foremost (al-sābiq), and that His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَهَا﴾ is for the moderate and the foremost. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, al-Ḥasan and Qatāda.
Ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ ظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِ﴾ — he said: an unbeliever.
And from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: ﴿الكِتَابُ﴾: every Book that was sent down.
And from him: all of them are the community of Muḥammad ﷺ — in the narration of Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa from him; and this is the most fitting of what has been said about it.
Al-Thawrī related from Jābir, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ثُمَّ أَوْرَثْنَا ٱلْكِتَابَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱصْطَفَيْنَا مِنْ عِبَادِنَا﴾ to the end of the verse.
He said: this is like His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَأَصْحَابُ المَيْمَنَةِ مَا أَصْحَابُ المَيْمَنَة. وَأَصْحَابُ المَشْأَمَةِ مَا أَصْحَابُ المَشْأَمَةِ. وَالسَّابِقُونَ السَّابِقُونَ أُوْلَئِكَ المُقَرَّبُونَ﴾.
He said: so two groups are saved.
Mujāhid said: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ ظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِ﴾ are the Companions of the Left; ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مُّقْتَصِدٌ وَمِنْهُمْ سَابِقٌ بِٱلْخَيْرَاتِ بِإِذُنِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ — the foremost among all people.
ʿIkrima said: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ ظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِ﴾ is as He said: ﴿فَذُوقُوا فَمَا للِظَّالِميِنَ مِنْ نَصِيرٍ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ ظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِ﴾ is the hypocrite.
Qatāda said: ﴿الكتابُ﴾ is the testimony that there is no god but Allah.
And it has been said: all three groups are saved. This was said by ʿUmar, Abū al-Dardāʾ, Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī and Kaʿb al-Aḥbār.
ʿUthmān said: they are the people of our desert — meaning the one who wrongs himself.
ʿUmar said: our foremost is foremost, our moderate is saved, and our wrongdoer is forgiven.
Abū al-Dardāʾ said: the foremost enters Paradise without reckoning; (the moderate) is given an easy reckoning; and (the one who wrongs himself) is taken to account and then saved — and that is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَقَالُوا الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الحَزَنَ﴾.
Kaʿb said: this community is in three groups, all of them in Paradise. Then he recited ﴿ثُمَّ أَوْرَثْنَا ٱلْكِتَابَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱصْطَفَيْنَا مِنْ عِبَادِنَا فَمِنْهُمْ ظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِ﴾ up to His saying ﴿جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَهَا﴾ and said: they have entered it, by the Lord of the Kaʿba.
And after this comes [what is] for the unbelievers.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
That is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَهُمْ نَارُ جَهَنَّمَ لاَ يُقْضَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَمُوتُواْ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: men are of four kinds: the generous, the miserly, the extravagant and the moderate.
The generous is the one who directs both the share of his Hereafter and the share of his worldly life, together, towards his Hereafter.
The miserly is the one who gives neither of them its due.
The extravagant is the one who gathers both of them for this world.
The moderate is the one who gives each of them its share, i.e. his deeds are measured (qaṣd), not strenuous. [Translator's note: the source reads «ليس يمجتهد», apparently a misprint for «ليس بمجتهد» "not strenuous"; translated accordingly.]
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the meaning of ﴿أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الحَزَنَ﴾ is: worry over livelihood, fear of the punishment, and the expectation of death.
And all that he said has come in the tafsīr, so it is general for every kind of grief.
Al-muqāma and al-maqām are the same; and al-naṣab is fatigue.
Al-lughūb is exhaustion; and al-laghūb, with fatḥa on the lām, is that from which one becomes exhausted.
Al-Ḥasan read: ﴿لا يُقْضَى عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَمُوتُونَ﴾.
The meaning according to his reading is: death is not decreed for them, and they do not die.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَوَلَمْ نُعَمِّرْكُمْ مَّا يَتَذَكَّرُ فِيهِ مَن تَذَكَّرَ﴾.
Abū Hurayra and Ibn ʿAbbās said: sixty years.
And from him [Ibn ʿAbbās] also: forty.
And this is more likely, because at forty the intellect reaches its full extent, and what is before and after that falls short of it — and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows best.
Al-Ḥasan also said: forty; and it is said that a seventeen-year-old is included in it.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَجَآءَكُمُ ٱلنَّذِيرُ﴾.
Ibn Zayd said: the Prophet ﷺ.
And it has been said: it means grey hair.
The first is held by more; and the meaning according to the second is: until you grew grey — and this is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَكُمْ خَلاَئِفَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
That is, you succeed those who were before you, and take warning from what befell them.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَمَن كَفَرَ فَعَلَيْهِ كُفْرُهُ﴾.
That is, the recompense of his unbelief.
﴿وَلاَ يَزِيدُ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ كُفْرُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ إِلاَّ مَقْتاً﴾.
Al-maqt is the most intense loathing.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ شُرَكَآءَكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
The meaning, according to Sībawayh: Inform me about those whom you call upon besides Allah — by way of making them stop and consider (tawqīf).
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿أَرُونِي مَاذَا خَلَقُواْ مِنَ ٱلأَرْضِ أَمْ لَهُمْ شِرْكٌ فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ﴾.
That is: did you worship them because they created something of the earth? Or do they have a share in the creation of the heavens?
﴿أَمْ آتَيْنَاهُمْ كِتَاباً﴾ granting partnership, ﴿فَهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍ مِّنْهُ﴾ — that is, upon clear proofs from it?

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُمْسِكُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ أَن تَزُولاَ﴾.
The meaning according to the Basrans: lest they cease (literally "from dislike that they cease"), just as He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿وَاسْأَلِ القَرْيَةَ﴾. [Translator's note: i.e. a muḍāf is omitted, as "the people of" is omitted in «واسأل القرية».]
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلَئِن زَالَتَآ إِنْ أَمْسَكَهُمَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِّن بَعْدِهِ﴾.
The meaning may be: at their ceasing on the Day of Resurrection.
And it may be that this is said even though they do not cease; "إنْ" is in the sense of "ما" (not). It resembles His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَئِنْ أَرْسَلْنَا رِيحَاً فَرَأَوْهُ مُصْفَرَّاً﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: there is a question about the verse. It is said: this is a context of power, so how did He say ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ حَلِيماً غَفُوراً﴾?
The answer: when they said ﴿اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمَنُ وَلَدَاً﴾, the mountains nearly ceased, the heavens nearly split apart and the earth nearly collapsed, because of the enormity of what they said; so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, held them still, delayed their punishment and was forbearing towards them. That is His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ حَلِيماً غَفُوراً﴾.

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لَئِن جَآءَهُمْ نَذِيرٌ لَّيَكُونُنَّ أَهْدَىٰ مِنْ إِحْدَى ٱلأُمَمِ﴾.
The meaning of ﴿أَهْدَىٰ مِنْ إِحْدَى ٱلأُمَمِ﴾ is: [better guided than] the Jews and the Christians.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ٱسْتِكْبَاراً فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَمَكْرَ ٱلسَّيِّىءِ وَلاَ يَحِيقُ ٱلْمَكْرُ ٱلسَّيِّىءُ إِلاَّ بِأَهْلِهِ﴾.
﴿وَمَكْرَ ٱلسَّيِّىءِ﴾: it has been said: that is, and the plotting of unbelief.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ يَحِيقُ ٱلْمَكْرُ ٱلسَّيِّىءُ إِلاَّ بِأَهْلِهِ﴾ — that is, the harm of the evil plot befalls none but its people, i.e. those who plot it.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَهَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلاَّ سُنَّتَ آلأَوَّلِينَ﴾? [verse 43].
That is: do they await anything but the way [of Allah] with the former peoples in punishment when they disbelieved?

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَوْ يُؤَاخِذُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّاسَ بِمَا كَسَبُواْ مَا تَرَكَ عَلَىٰ ظَهْرِهَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: it means people specifically.
And from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd there is what indicates that it means people and others.
He said: the dung beetle was nearly punished for the sin of the children of Adam. Then he recited ﴿وَلَوْ يُؤَاخِذُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّاسَ بِمَا كَسَبُواْ مَا تَرَكَ عَلَىٰ ظَهْرِهَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ﴾, the verse.
Qatāda said: that was done in the days of Noah ﷺ.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿عَلَىٰ ظَهْرِهَا﴾.
It has been said: it is known that the meaning is "on the surface of the earth".
Abū Jaʿfar said: it is better that the pronoun refer back to what has already been mentioned, in His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الأَرْضِ﴾.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِ بَصِيراً﴾.
﴿فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمْ﴾: that is, the term of their punishment.
﴿فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِ بَصِيراً﴾: that is, All-Seeing of what each group of them deserves.

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلْحَمْدُ للَّهِ فَاطِرِ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: I did not know what ﴿فاطرُ﴾ meant until two Bedouins brought a dispute to me over a well, and one of them said: I فَطَرْتُها, that is, I began it.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿جَاعِلِ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةِ رُسُلاً أُوْلِيۤ أَجْنِحَةٍ مَّثْنَىٰ وَثُلاَثَ وَرُبَاعَ﴾.
The messengers among them are "Gabriel, Michael, Isrāfīl and the Angel of Death", may Allah bless them.
* His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أُوْلِيۤ أَجْنِحَةٍ مَّثْنَىٰ وَثُلاَثَ وَرُبَاعَ﴾, that is, possessors of wings: two by two, three by three and four by four, on each side.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يَزِيدُ فِي ٱلْخَلْقِ مَا يَشَآءُ﴾.
That is, He adds to the creation of the angels whatever He wills.
Al-Zuhrī said: ﴿يَزِيدُ فِي ٱلْخَلْقِ مَا يَشَآءُ﴾: a beautiful voice.
The first is preferable.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَّا يَفْتَحِ ٱللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ مِن رَّحْمَةٍ فَلاَ مُمْسِكَ لَهَا﴾.
That is, whatever Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, brings of rain and provision, no one is able to turn it back.
Qatāda said: ﴿مِن رَّحْمَةٍ﴾: of good; no one is able to withhold it.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿لاَ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ فَأَنَّىٰ تُؤْفَكُونَ﴾.
That is: so how are you turned away from [affirming His] oneness and from belief in the resurrection, after the proofs and the signs?

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلاَ تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ ٱلْحَيَاةُ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَلاَ يَغُرَّنَّكُمْ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلْغَرُورُ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: ﴿ٱلْغَرُورُ﴾ is Satan.
Shuʿba narrated from Simāk ibn Ḥarb: ﴿الغُرُورُ﴾ with ḍamma on the ghayn.
It was said: This is not permissible, because one only says غرَّه غرَّاً, and the maṣdar (verbal noun) hardly ever comes on the pattern "فُعُول" with a transitive verb except anomalously.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is possible that "غُرُور" is the plural of غارّ (deceiver), or the plural of غِرّ (one who is deceived); or it may be likened to their saying نَهَكَه المرضُ نُهُوكاً (illness wore him down) and لَزِمَه لُزُوماً (it clung to him).

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَمَن زُيِّنَ لَهُ سُوۤءُ عَمَلِهِ فَرَآهُ حَسَناً﴾.
The answer (complement) is omitted because the hearer knows it. The meaning may be: Is one to whom the evil of his deed has been made to seem fair like one whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has guided? And what indicates this omitted [part] would be ﴿فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِي مَن يَشَآءُ﴾.
And the meaning may be: Is one to whom the evil of his deed has been made to seem fair [one over whom] your soul should waste away [in grief]?
And what indicates it would be ﴿فَلاَ تَذْهَبْ نَفْسُكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَسَرَاتٍ﴾.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ ٱلْعِزَّةَ فَلِلَّهِ ٱلْعِزَّةُ جَمِيعاً﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: Whoever seeks might through the worship of idols.
Al-Farrāʾ said: Whoever seeks to know [to whom] might [belongs].
Then He said: ﴿فَلِلَّهِ ٱلْعِزَّةُ جَمِيعاً﴾, that is, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, gives might to whomever He wills through obedience to Him.
Qatāda said: So let him seek might through obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The most fitting of them is the first, because in the verses before it the polytheists were rebuked for worshipping idols, so it is more fitting that this one too be of the kind that urges abandoning that.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ ٱلْكَلِمُ ٱلطَّيِّبُ وَٱلْعَمَلُ ٱلصَّالِحُ يَرْفَعُهُ﴾.
Concerning its meaning there are three views:
A- Among them is what Bakr ibn Sahl narrated to us; he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying ﴿إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ ٱلْكَلِمُ ٱلطَّيِّبُ وَٱلْعَمَلُ ٱلصَّالِحُ يَرْفَعُهُ﴾: he said: The good speech is the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and ﴿ٱلْعَمَلُ ٱلصَّالِحُ﴾ is the performance of His obligations.
So whoever remembers Allah, Glorified is He, while performing His obligations, his deed carries the remembrance of Allah and it ascends to Allah, Glorified is He.
And whoever remembers Allah but does not perform His obligations, his speech is turned back upon his deed, and [his deed] has the greater claim on him.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Likewise said al-Ḥasan, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, Abū al-ʿĀliya and al-Ḍaḥḥāk; they said: The righteous deed raises the good speech.
Al-Ḥasan said: If there is good speech but an evil deed, the saying is turned back upon the deed, and your deed has a greater claim on you than your saying.
B- Shahr ibn Ḥawshab said: ﴿إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ ٱلْكَلِمُ ٱلطَّيِّبُ﴾ is the Qurʾān; ﴿وَٱلْعَمَلُ ٱلصَّالِحُ يَرْفَعُهُ﴾: the Qurʾān [raises it].
C- Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: And the righteous deed — Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, raises it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Qatāda's view is not far-fetched in meaning, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, raises deeds.
And the meaning of Shahr ibn Ḥawshab's view is that the righteous deed does not benefit you except together with tawḥīd (affirming Allah's oneness), so it is as though tawḥīd raises it.
However, the first view is the most fitting and the soundest of them, because of the high standing of those who held it, and because it is more fitting in Arabic: the readers have the nominative for العمل; had the meaning been "and the righteous deed, Allah raises it" or "and the righteous deed, the good word raises it", the preferred choice would have been the accusative for العمل. We do not know of anyone who read it in the accusative, except something narrated from ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, who said: Some people read it ﴿والعملَ الصالحَ يرفعهُ﴾.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَمْكُرُونَ ٱلسَّيِّئَاتِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَكْرُ أُوْلَئِكَ هُوَ يَبُورُ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: ﴿يَبُورُ﴾: he said: comes to ruin.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has made this plotting clear in His saying: ﴿وَإذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِيُثْبِتُوكَ﴾.
Qays narrated from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid: ﴿وَمَكْرُ أُوْلَئِكَ هُوَ يَبُورُ﴾: he said: showing off (riyāʾ).

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا يُعَمَّرُ مِن مُّعَمَّرٍ وَلاَ يُنقَصُ مِنْ عُمُرِهِ إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ﴾.
Concerning the meaning of this verse there are [several] views:
A- Among the best of them and the closest to the apparent sense of the revelation is the view of al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: "Whomever I have decreed to be given long life until old age overtakes him, or to be given a life short of that — all of that is by decree, and all is in a Book."
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning on this view is: ﴿وَمَا يُعَمَّرُ مِن مُّعَمَّرٍ﴾, that is, an aged one — and "so-and-so is مُعَمَّر" means old — ﴿وَلاَ يُنقَصُ﴾ another ﴿مِنْ عُمُرِهِ﴾, from the lifespan of the aged one, except by a decree from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
B- ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَمَا يُعَمَّرُ مِن مُّعَمَّرٍ وَلاَ يُنقَصُ مِنْ عُمُرِهِ إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ﴾:
He said: His lifespan is written as so many years, so many months and so many days; then it is written: a day has been subtracted from his life, a month has been subtracted from his life, a year has been subtracted from his life — in another record — until he completes his term and dies.
C- Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: What has passed of his life is the subtraction, and what is yet to come is that for which he is given life.
D- Al-Zuhrī narrated from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Kaʿb al-Aḥbār, that he said, when ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was stabbed: "If he were to supplicate to Allah, He would extend his term." The Muslims objected to him about that and said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, says: ﴿فإذَا جَاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ لاَ يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ سَاعَةً وَلا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ﴾. He said: And Allah, Exalted is He, says: ﴿وَمَا يُعَمَّرُ مِن مُّعَمَّرٍ وَلاَ يُنقَصُ مِنْ عُمُرِهِ إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ﴾.
E- Al-Zuhrī said: We hold that it may be deferred as long as the term has not arrived; but when the term arrives, nothing is added to the lifespan and no deferral occurs.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It has also been said concerning the meaning of the verse: it may be that it is decreed that a person's lifespan is a hundred years if he obeys and ninety if he disobeys; whichever of the two he reaches is in a Book.
﴿إِنَّ ذَلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ﴾, that is, recording long and short lifespans is not difficult for Him.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا يَسْتَوِي ٱلْبَحْرَانِ هَـٰذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: الفُرَات is the sweetest of sweet [water], and الأُجَاج is the saltiest of salt.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَمِن كُلٍّ تَأْكُلُونَ لَحْماً طَرِيّاً وَتَسْتَخْرِجُونَ حِلْيَةً تَلْبَسُونَهَا﴾.
The ornament is pearls and coral, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالمَرْجَانُ﴾, although they come out only from the salt [sea].
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is frequent in the speech of the Arabs: because the two seas are mixed, it is permissible to say "it comes out of both of them" although it comes out only of one of them — according to the view of some lexicographers.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَتَرَى ٱلْفُلْكَ فِيهِ مَوَاخِرَ لِتَبْتَغُواْ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, the ships run coming and going.
