It is also possible that it is ”يُحَلَّوْنَ مِن أساوِرَ مِن ذَهَبٍ“ and ”يُحَلَّوْنَ مِن لُؤْلُؤٍ“; and it is permissible in the sense of ”وَيُحَلَّوْنَ لُؤْلُؤًا“. ”أساوِرُ“ is the plural of ”إسْوِرَةٌ“, and ”أساوِرُ“ — its singular is siwār. ”اَلْأُسْوارُ“, from the asāwira of the Persians, is the one who is skilled at shooting arrows. The poet said:
؎وَوَتَّرَ الأساوِرُ القِياسا ∗∗∗ سَعْدِيَّةٌ تَنْتَزِعُ الأنْفاسا
(And the Persian archers strung the bows — Saʿdī bows that snatch away the breaths.)

zajjaj:34-34.t: ﴿وَقالُوا الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أذْهَبَ عَنّا الحَزَنَ﴾ ("and they will say: Praise be to Allah who has removed grief from us"). ”اَلْحُزْنُ“ is also permissible, like ”اَلرُّشْدُ“ and ”اَلرَّشَدُ“, and ”اَلْعُرْبُ“ and ”اَلْعَرَبُ“. The meaning of ”أذْهَبَ عَنّا الحَزَنَ“ is: He has removed from us everything that grieves — grief over livelihood, or grief over punishment, or grief over death; and Allah has removed every grief from the people of Paradise. [Translator's note: the printed word مَقاسٍ is rendered here as "livelihood" on the assumption that مَعاشٍ is intended; it may be a misprint.]

zajjaj:35-35.t: ﴿الَّذِي أحَلَّنا دارَ المُقامَةِ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾ ("who has settled us in the Abode of Permanent Stay out of His bounty"): [المُقامَة is] like al-iqāma (staying); you say: ”أقَمْتُ بِالمَكانِ، إقامَةً، ومَقامَةً، ومُقامًا“ ("I stayed in the place"). That is: He has settled us in the abode of eternity out of His bounty, that is: that is by His favour, not by our deeds. ﴿لا يَمَسُّنا فِيها نَصَبٌ﴾ ("no toil touches us therein"), that is: fatigue. ﴿وَلا يَمَسُّنا فِيها لُغُوبٌ﴾ ("nor does weariness touch us therein"): ”اَللُّغُوبُ“ is exhaustion from fatigue. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read: ”لَغُوبٌ“, with fatḥa on the lām, and the ḍamma is more common. The meaning of ”لَغُوبٌ“ is: something from which one becomes weary, that is: we do not burden ourselves with anything from which we become exhausted.

zajjaj:36-36.t: ﴿والَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَهم نارُ جَهَنَّمَ لا يُقْضى عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَمُوتُوا﴾ ("and those who disbelieve will have the Fire of Hell; it will not be decreed for them that they die"). ”فَيَمُوتُوا“ is accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the dropping of the nūn; it is the answer to the negation. The meaning is: "death will not be decreed for them so that they die". ﴿وَلا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهم مِن عَذابِها﴾ ("nor will its punishment be lightened for them"), that is: the punishment of the Fire of Hell. ﴿كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي كُلَّ كَفُورٍ﴾ ("thus do We recompense every ungrateful one"), and [also read] ”يُجْزى كُلُّ كَفُورٍ“. There is a third way in it: ”كَذَلِكَ يَجْزِي كُلَّ كَفُورٍ“, that is: "thus does Allah recompense…". The meaning is: "like that recompense which We have mentioned". I do not know anyone who read it so — I mean ”يَجْزِي“ with the yāʾ and with its fatḥa.

zajjaj:37-37.t: ﴿وَهم يَصْطَرِخُونَ فِيها﴾ ("and they will cry out therein"): they call for help: "Our Lord, bring us out!" The meaning is: "they say: Our Lord, bring us out, we will do righteous deeds other than what we used to do"; the meaning is: "if You bring us out, we will do righteous deeds". So Allah rebuked them and said: ﴿أوَلَمْ نُعَمِّرْكم ما يَتَذَكَّرُ فِيهِ مَن تَذَكَّرَ﴾ ("did We not give you life long enough for whoever would remember to remember therein?"). Its meaning is: "Did We not give you the life-span in which whoever would remember could remember?!" It has come in the exegesis: "Allah has left no excuse to a servant whose life reaches sixty years", and it is said: "from sixty to seventy". It has also come in the exegesis that one of seventeen years is included in it, and it has been said: "forty". ﴿وَجاءَكُمُ النَّذِيرُ﴾ ("and the warner came to you"): meaning the Prophet ﷺ; and it has been said: grey hair. The first view, that the Prophet ﷺ is the warner, is what most exegesis holds. And it has been said: "forty".

zajjaj:38-38.t: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ عالِمُ غَيْبِ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾ ("Allah is the Knower of the unseen of the heavens and the earth"). The common reading is with the genitive (khafḍ). It is permissible [to say]: ”عالِمٌ غَيْبَ السَّماواتِ“, in the sense of ”يَعْلَمُ“ ("He knows"); and ”عالِمٌ غَيْبَ“ in the sense of ”قَدْ عَلِمَ ذَلِكَ“ ("He has known that").

zajjaj:39-39.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَكم خَلائِفَ في الأرْضِ﴾ ("it is He who made you successors in the earth"). ”خَلائِفَ“ is the plural of ”خَلِيفَةً“. The meaning is: "He made you a community that succeeded those before it, and saw and witnessed, in those who went before, what ought to be taken as a lesson". ﴿فَمَن كَفَرَ فَعَلَيْهِ كُفْرُهُ﴾ ("so whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief"): the meaning is: "upon him is the recompense of his disbelief". ﴿وَلا يَزِيدُ الكافِرِينَ كُفْرُهم عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ إلا مَقْتًا﴾ ("and their disbelief does not increase the unbelievers with their Lord except in maqt"): "maqt is the most intense loathing".

zajjaj:40-40.t:
﴿قُلْ أرَأيْتُمْ شُرَكاءَكُمُ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ﴾ ("say: Have you considered your partners whom you call upon"): its meaning is: "Say: Tell me about your partners."
﴿ماذا خَلَقُوا مِنَ الأرْضِ﴾ ("what have they created of the earth?"): the meaning is: "On what ground have you assigned to them partnership with Allah? Is it for something they created of the earth?" ﴿أمْ لَهم شِرْكٌ في السَّماواتِ أمْ آتَيْناهم كِتابًا﴾ ("or do they have a share in the heavens, or have We given them a Book"), that is: or have We given them a Book supporting the partnership they claim? ﴿فَهم عَلى بَيِّنَتٍ مِنهُ﴾ ("so that they are upon clear evidence from it"), and it is also read: ”بَيِّناتٍ“. ﴿بَلْ إنْ يَعِدُ الظّالِمُونَ بَعْضُهم بَعْضًا إلا غُرُورًا﴾ ("rather the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion"). ”اَلْغُرُورُ“ is the falsehoods that delude. The meaning of ”إنْ يَعِدُ“ is ”ما يَعِدُ“ ("they do not promise"), and ”بَعْضُهم“ is a badal (substitute) for ”اَلظّالِمِينَ“.

zajjaj:41-41.t: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يُمْسِكُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ أنْ تَزُولا﴾ ("Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease"). The meaning of ”يُمْسِكُ“ is: He prevents the heavens and the earth from ceasing. When the Christians said: "The Messiah is the son of Allah", and the Jews said: "ʿUzayr is the son of Allah", the heavens were about to burst apart because of it, the mountains were about to cease, and the earth was about to split. Allah said: ﴿وَقالُوا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمَنُ ولَدًا﴾ [Maryam: 88] ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْئًا إدًّا﴾ [Maryam: 89] — the three verses — so Allah held them. He said ”اَلسَّماواتِ والأرْضَ“ [with the earth in the singular] because "the earth" indicates the earths. ﴿وَلَئِنْ زالَتا إنْ أمْسَكَهُما مِن أحَدٍ مِن بَعْدِهِ﴾ ("and if they were to cease, no one could hold them after Him"): this admits — and Allah knows best — two ways of answer. One of them: "their ceasing at the Resurrection"; Allah said: ﴿وَإذا السَّماءُ كُشِطَتْ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 11]. And it may be said that [it says] ”زالَتا“ while they do not cease. As for His saying in this place: ﴿إنَّهُ كانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورًا﴾ ("indeed He is Forbearing, Forgiving"), some people asked and said: why is there mention of forbearance and forgiveness in this place, when this is a place indicating power? The answer to this is that when He held the heavens and the earth at their saying "The Most Merciful has taken a son", [that was] forbearance: He did not hasten the punishment for them, and He held the heavens and the earth lest they cease because of the enormity of their fabrication.

zajjaj:42-42.t: ﴿وَأقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أيْمانِهِمْ﴾ ("and they swore by Allah their most solemn oaths"): meaning the polytheists. They had sworn and done their utmost: ﴿لَئِنْ جاءَهم نَذِيرٌ لَيَكُونُنَّ أهْدى مِن إحْدى الأُمَمِ﴾ ("that if a warner came to them they would be better guided than any of the nations"), that is: than the Jews, the Christians and others. ﴿فَلَمّا جاءَهم نَذِيرٌ﴾ ("but when a warner came to them") — and he is Muḥammad ﷺ — ﴿ما زادَهم إلا نُفُورًا﴾ ("it increased them only in aversion"): only in that they fled from the truth.

zajjaj:43-43.t:
﴿اسْتِكْبارًا في الأرْضِ﴾ ("out of arrogance in the land"). ”اِسْتِكْبارًا“ is accusative (manṣūb), a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). The meaning is: "it increased them only in fleeing out of arrogance".
﴿وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ﴾ ("and the plotting of evil"), that is: the plotting of polytheism. ﴿وَلا يَحِيقُ﴾: [it does not] encompass. Ḥamza read: ”وَلا يَحِيقُ المَكْرُ السَّيِّئْ“, with a pause [i.e. a sukūn on the hamza]. According to the skilled grammarians this is a solecism (laḥn) and is not permissible; the like of it is permissible only in poetry, under metrical necessity. The poet said:
؎إذا اعْوَجَجْنَ قُلْتُ صاحِبْ قَوِّمِ
(When they [the camels] veer off course, I say: "Companion, set them straight!")
The original is ”يا صاحِبُ قَوِّمِ“, but he elided [the vowel] out of necessity; there was a ḍamma after a kasra, and a kasra after a kasra is felt to be heavy. They also recited:
؎فاليَوْمَ أشْرَبْ غَيْرَ مُسْتَحْقِبٍ ∗∗∗ إثْمًا مِنَ اللَّهِ ولا واغِلِ
(So today I drink, not burdening myself with a sin before Allah, nor as an uninvited intruder.)
These two verses have been recited by all the grammarians mentioned, and they all held that this is metrical necessity in poetry and that the like of it is not permissible in the Book of Allah. Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] — may Allah have mercy on him — recited them to us as:
؎إذا اعْوَجَجْنَ قُلْتُ صاحٍ قَوِّمِ
(When they veer off course, I say: "Friend, set them straight!")
and this is excellent and perfect; and he recited to us:
؎فاليَوْمَ فاشْرَبْ غَيْرَ مُسْتَحْقِبٍ
(So today, drink, not burdening yourself…)
As for what is related from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ in his reading ”إلى بارِئْكم“, it is only that he slurs the kasra (ikhtilās), and does not give ”بارِئِكم“ a sukūn. This — I mean the sukūn of بارِئِكم — was only related from Abū ʿAmr by someone who does not master grammar as Sībawayh and al-Khalīl master it; Sībawayh related it with a slurred kasra, as though he reduced his voice at the kasra.
﴿فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إلا سُنَّتَ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ ("then do they await anything but the way of the former peoples?"): its meaning is: "Do they await anything but the like of the days of those who passed away before them?!", and the meaning is: "Do they await anything but that there should descend upon them the like of the punishment that descended upon those before them?!"

zajjaj:44-44.t: ﴿وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعْجِزَهُ مِن شَيْءٍ﴾ ("and Allah is not such that anything could thwart Him"): the meaning is: "that anything of the affair of the heavens or of the affair of the earth could escape Him".

zajjaj:45-45.t:
﴿وَلَوْ يُؤاخِذُ اللَّهُ النّاسَ بِما كَسَبُوا ما تَرَكَ عَلى ظَهْرِها مِن دابَّةٍ﴾ ("and if Allah were to take people to task for what they have earned, He would not leave upon its back any creature"). They said: He said ”عَلى ظَهْرِها“ ("upon its back") because the meaning makes it known that it is upon the back of the earth. The truth of this is that mention of the earth has already occurred, in His saying in the verse before this one, which immediately precedes it: ﴿وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعْجِزَهُ مِن شَيْءٍ في السَّماواتِ ولا في الأرْضِ﴾ [Fāṭir: 44]; that is why ”عَلى ظَهْرِها“ came.
And His saying: ﴿ما تَرَكَ عَلى ظَهْرِها مِن دابَّةٍ﴾ — there are two views on it. It has been said: "any creature among humans and jinn and every being that reasons"; and it has come from Ibn Masʿūd: "The dung-beetle almost perishes in its hole because of the sin of the son of Adam" — and this indicates generality. What has come [in the view] that humans and jinn are meant by it seems more likely — and Allah knows best.
End of the Sūra of "al-Malāʾika" (the Angels).

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Malāʾika (The Angels)
Meccan
﷽
﴿الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ فاطِرِ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾: Ibn ʿAbbās — may Allah have mercy on him — said: “I did not know what “ فاطِرِ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ ” meant until two Bedouins brought a dispute to me over a well, and one of them said: “ أنا فَطَرْتُها ” (I originated it), that is: I began it. It is said: ﴿فاطِرِ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾ [means] “ Creator of the heavens and the earth ”. “ فاطِرُ ” and “ فاطِرَ ”, in the nominative and the accusative, are permissible, but the reading is with “ فاطِرِ ” in the genitive; and likewise ﴿جاعِلِ المَلائِكَةِ رُسُلا أُولِي أجْنِحَةٍ مَثْنى وثُلاثَ ورُباعَ﴾. The meaning of “ أُولِي ” is: possessors of wings. “ ثُلاثَ ورُباعَ ” are in the position of the “ genitive ”, and likewise “ مَثْنى ”, except that “ ثُلاثَ ورُباعَ ” take fatḥa because they are diptotes (lā yanṣarif) for two reasons. One of them is that they are deflected (maʿdūl) from “ ثَلاثَةً ثَلاثَةً ” (three by three), “ أرْبَعَةً أرْبَعَةً ” (four by four) and “ اِثْنَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ " (two by two); this is one reason. The second reason is that the deflection occurred while it is indefinite. The poet said:
وَلَكِنَّما أهْلِي بِوادٍ أنِيسُهُ ∗∗∗ ذِئابٌ تَبَغّى النّاسَ مَثْنى ومَوْحَدا
(But my people are in a valley whose only company is wolves that seek people out in twos and singly.)
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يَزِيدُ في الخَلْقِ ما يَشاءُ﴾: He means in the creation of the angels. The messengers from among the angels are Gabriel, Michael, Isrāfīl and the Angel of Death.

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿ما يَفْتَحِ اللَّهُ لِلنّاسِ مِن رَحْمَةٍ فَلا مُمْسِكَ لَها﴾: ”يَفْتَحِ“ is in the position of the jussive, on the meaning of condition and response (al-sharṭ wa-l-jazāʾ), and the answer to the condition is: ”فَلا مُمْسِكَ لَها“. Had it been ”فَلا مُمْسِكَ لَهُ“, it would have been permissible, because ”ما“ is masculine in wording; but since mention of mercy had occurred, ”فَلا مُمْسِكَ لَها“ was better. Do you not see His words: ﴿وَما يُمْسِكْ فَلا مُرْسِلَ لَهُ مِن بَعْدِهِ﴾?! The meaning of ”ما يَفْتَحِ اللَّهُ“ is: "Whatever rain and provision He brings them, no one is able to withhold it; and whatever of that Allah withholds, no one with power is able to release it." It is also permissible — though I know of no one who read it — ”ما يَفْتَحُ اللَّهُ لِلنّاسِ مِن رَحْمَةٍ“ and ”ما يُمْسِكُ“, both in the nominative, on the meaning: "What Allah opens to people of mercy, there is none to withhold it, and what He withholds, there is none to release it." ”فَلا مُمْسِكٌ لَها“ with nunation is also permissible, and ”ما يُمْسِكْ فَلا مُرْسِلٌ لَهُ مِن بَعْدِهِ“, but I know of no one who read so; so do not read what has no established transmission, even if it occurs in Arabic, because reading [the Quran] is a sunna (an established practice).

zajjaj:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿هَلْ مِن خالِقٍ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَرْزُقُكُمْ﴾: this is mentioned after His words: ﴿ما يَفْتَحِ اللَّهُ لِلنّاسِ مِن رَحْمَةٍ فَلا مُمْسِكَ لَها﴾ [Fāṭir: 2], and He emphasized that by putting the question to them: "Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?" It has been read: ﴿هَلْ مِن خالِقٍ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ﴾ in the nominative, with ”غَيْرُ“ in the nominative, the meaning being: "Is there a creator other than Allah?", because ”مِن“ is emphatic. Both have been read: ”غَيْرُ“ and ”غَيْرِ“. There is another way in it: in Arabic the accusative of ”غَيْرُ“ is permissible: ”هَلْ مِن خالِقٍ غَيْرَ اللَّهِ يَرْزُقُكم“, the accusative being by exception, as though [it were]: "Is there any creator except Allah who provides for you?!"
﴿فَأنّى تُؤْفَكُونَ﴾, that is: "From where does the deception befall you, and the denial of the oneness of Allah and the rejection of the resurrection?!"

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿وَإنْ يُكَذِّبُوكَ فَقَدْ كُذِّبَتْ رُسُلٌ مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾: this is a consolation for the Prophet ﷺ. Allah informed him that messengers before him had been denied, and informed him that He helped them, saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَصَبَرُوا عَلى ما كُذِّبُوا وأُوذُوا حَتّى أتاهم نَصْرُنا﴾ [al-Anʿām: 34]. ﴿وَإلى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الأُمُورُ﴾, and ”تَرْجِعُ الأُمُورُ“ [is also read]; the meaning is: "The matter returns to Allah in recompensing those who denied and in helping those of His messengers who were denied."

zajjaj:5-5.t: His words: ﴿يا أيُّها النّاسُ إنَّ وعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ﴾, that is: "What Allah has promised you of recompense is true." ﴿فَلا تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ الحَياةُ الدُّنْيا﴾, that is: even if you have a share in this world that detracts from your religion, do not prefer that share. ﴿وَلا يَغُرَّنَّكم بِاللَّهِ الغَرُورُ﴾: ”اَلْغَرُورُ“ is Satan. It is also read: ”اَلْغُرُورُ“ with ḍamma on the ghayn, which is vain things (al-abāṭīl). ”اَلْغُرُورُ“ may be the plural of ”غارٌّ“ (deceiver), [as] ”غُرُورٌ“, like ”قاعِدٌ“ and ”قُعُودٌ“. It may be the plural of ”غَرٌّ“, the maṣdar of ”غَرَرْتُهُ، غَرًّا“. As for its being the maṣdar of ”غَرَرْتُهُ، غُرُورًا“, that is far-fetched, because transitive verbs hardly ever have their maṣdars on the pattern ”فُعُولٌ“; yet some of them have come on ”فُعُولٌ“, such as ”لَزِمْتُهُ، لُزُومًا“ and ”نَهِكَهُ المَرَضُ، نُهُوكًا“ (the illness wasted him), so ”غَرَرْتُهُ، غُرُورًا“ is permissible on that basis.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His words, the Exalted: ﴿أفَمَن زُيِّنَ لَهُ سُوءُ عَمَلِهِ فَرَآهُ حَسَنًا فَإنَّ اللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَن يَشاءُ﴾: the answer here is of two kinds. One of them is indicated by ”فَلا تَذْهَبْ نَفْسُكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَسَراتٍ“, the meaning being: "Is the one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him, so that Allah has led him astray — has your soul gone out in grief for him?", with ”فَلا تَذْهَبْ نَفْسُكَ“ indicating it. It has been read: ”فَلا تُذْهِبْ نَفْسَكَ“ with ḍamma on the tāʾ, the bāʾ in the jussive and nafs in the accusative. It may also be that the answer is omitted, the meaning being: "Is the one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him like one whom Allah has guided?", its indication being: ﴿فَإنَّ اللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَن يَشاءُ ويَهْدِي مَن يَشاءُ﴾

zajjaj:9-9.t: His words: ﴿فَسُقْناهُ إلى بَلَدٍ مَيِّتٍ﴾, and ”مَيْتٍ“ [is also read]. ﴿فَأحْيَيْنا بِهِ الأرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها كَذَلِكَ النُّشُورُ﴾, that is: We bring forth anew. The meaning is: "like that", that is: like the reviving of the earth, so is your resurrection.

zajjaj:10-10.t:
﴿مَن كانَ يُرِيدُ العِزَّةَ فَلِلَّهِ العِزَّةُ جَمِيعًا﴾, that is: "Whoever seeks might by his worship of other than Allah — to Allah belongs all might", that is: in its being all together, that is: it comes together for Him in this world and the Hereafter. Then He made clear how one gains might through Allah, saying: ﴿إلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ الكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ والعَمَلُ الصّالِحُ يَرْفَعُهُ﴾, that is: to Him reaches the word which is the affirmation of the oneness of Allah, namely the saying "There is no god but Allah". ﴿والعَمَلُ الصّالِحُ يَرْفَعُهُ﴾: the meaning is: "When he affirms the oneness of Allah and hastens to obey Him, that rises to Allah — and to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, everything rises, and He knows everything." But the meaning in it here is: righteous action is what raises the mention of tawḥīd, so that it confirms for the one who affirms oneness the reality of tawḥīd. The pronoun in ”يَرْفَعُهُ“ may be one of three things, and that is the view of all the linguists. It may be: "and righteous action raises the good word"; it may be: "and righteous action, the good word raises it", that is: "righteous action is accepted only from one who affirms oneness"; and the third view is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, raises it.
﴿والَّذِينَ يَمْكُرُونَ السَّيِّئاتِ لَهم عَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ﴾: the meaning is: “the scheming of those who scheme against the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿هُوَ يَبُورُ﴾, that is: it comes to ruin. He has made clear what their scheming was in Sūrat “ al-Anfāl ", in His words: ﴿وَإذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِيُثْبِتُوكَ أوْ يَقْتُلُوكَ أوْ يُخْرِجُوكَ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 30]. So all their scheming came to ruin, and Allah made the word of His Prophet and His allies uppermost and their hands supreme, through victory and proof.
